judged_text: The decrypted keys payload is persisted without validating it against the target app's credential schema (each app ships one, e.g. googleCredentialSchema), and a decryption or JSON.parse failure surfaces as an unhandled 500. Parent/child version skew or a buggy parent silently persists malformed credentials that only fail at booking time, far from the write that caused them; a schema parse at this boundary would reject bad payloads with a 400.

adjudication.rationale: In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the decrypted `keys` are produced via `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""))` with no try/catch. If decryption fails (e.g., wrong key, malformed ciphertext) or JSON.parse fails, the handler will throw and Next.js will return an unhandled 500. Also, the resulting `keys` object is written directly to `prisma.credential.update/create` as `key: keys` without validating against any app-specific credential schema (only `appStoreMetadata` is consulted, which provides `slug`/`type` but no schema validation). This matches the finding that malformed payloads could be persisted and only fail later.
